assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened a new, highly tunable platform for strongly correlated electron physics and spawned the whole moire-materials field. It is a clean experimental discovery with a clear theoretical prediction, which fits the discovery-or-invention criterion well.
assessment.attribution: The 2018 experiments by Jarillo-Herrero and collaborators and the 2011 continuum-model prediction of the magic angle by Bistritzer and MacDonald form a natural three-person configuration. Other experimental contributors (e.g. the early graphene-twist work) are not in the credited list, so allocation is incomplete but supportable.
assessment.maturity: Many independent groups have reproduced the phases, and sample-quality and device-scale questions are well understood from a materials perspective, though the microscopic origin of superconductivity is still debated. Recognition is timely rather than premature.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism of the superconductivity remains unsettled.
Sample inhomogeneity and twist-angle disorder complicate comparison between devices.
Credit among experimental and theoretical contributors beyond the three names could be contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED realised strong light-matter coupling on a chip, giving the architecture for superconducting qubit readout, control and scaling, and is the base of present quantum processors. It is an invention with proven lasting impact and a clear identity as a discovery in solid-state quantum optics.
assessment.attribution: Blais and colleagues proposed the architecture in 2004, and Wallraff and Schoelkopf demonstrated strong coupling in the same year. This is a tidy prediction-plus-experiment pairing. Schoelkopf's group developed much of the subsequent toolbox, so credit weights are reasonably clear.
assessment.maturity: The concept is two decades old with extensive independent confirmation across many laboratories. The 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits is a related but distinct topic, so timing is mature without being repetitive.
uncertainties: Overlap with the recently recognised superconducting-circuit prize may weigh on committee appetite.
Contributions of other early circuit-quantum-device groups are not on the supplied list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction and observation of the quantum spin Hall effect and the realisation of the quantum anomalous Hall effect established topological insulators as a major class of materials. The impact on condensed-matter physics and materials design is large and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Kane (with Mele) provided the theory, Molenkamp the HgTe quantum spin Hall observation, and Xue the quantum anomalous Hall experiment. This is a plausible three-person split, but it excludes Mele, Zhang, Bernevig and others whose theory was decisive; the supplied credit therefore leaves an allocation problem.
assessment.maturity: Extensive independent confirmation exists in many materials. The field is mature, and recognition is not premature, though the multiplicity of contributors makes a clean prize difficult.
uncertainties: Theoretical priority among Kane, Mele, Bernevig, Zhang and others is disputed.
Whether a combined entry should be split into separate discoveries.
Material quality in magnetic topological insulators limits the quantisation temperature.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The proposal for quantum gates with trapped ions and its experimental realisation showed that a scalable, controlled quantum processor is possible, and trapped ions remain a leading quantum computing and simulation platform. The importance and originality are high.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller made the 1995 proposal, and Blatt's group implemented multi-ion entanglement and gates at high fidelity. Wineland and Monroe were important experimentally but Wineland has already been recognised, and Monroe is not on the list, so this three-person configuration is supportable but incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Experiments have been confirmed by many groups and the technology is commercially developed. Timing is mature, though there is overlap with another ballot entry covering atomic quantum information processing.
uncertainties: Overlap with the other atomic quantum-information entry on the longlist.
Omission of key experimental contributors who are not in the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on the magic-wavelength concept, brought a leap in precision timekeeping with fractional uncertainties near 1e-18, enabling tests of fundamental physics and relativistic geodesy. It is a concrete invention with a measurable impact.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice idea and Ye's group made the most precise realisations. The two names give a clear and compact allocation. Hall and Haensch were recognised in 2005 for frequency combs, which are a related enabling tool.
assessment.maturity: Many independent clocks agree at the 1e-18 level and the redefinition of the second is under discussion. This is mature and timely, though practical redefinition has not yet happened.
uncertainties: Whether the ongoing redefinition of the SI second would strengthen the case.
Other lattice clock groups are not credited here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Detection of a diffuse high-energy astrophysical neutrino flux and the first source associations at IceCube opened neutrino astronomy at TeV-PeV energies. This is an experimental discovery and a major instrumental achievement in astroparticle physics.
assessment.attribution: Halzen led the IceCube concept and project and Karle was a key figure in the detector's design and operation. The credited list is only two names, but IceCube is a large collaboration and the choice of individuals is difficult. The prize rules still allow it, though some members may be reluctant.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is well established and the first source candidates (the blazar TXS 0506+056 and NGC 1068) have been observed but the identification of the source populations is still incomplete. Recognition is possible but may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Collaboration credit and the role of other IceCube leaders and predecessors such as Antares or Baikal are unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Metal-halide perovskite solar cells rose from a few percent to above 25 percent efficiency within about a decade, a remarkable development in photovoltaic materials. As a materials physicist I find the defect tolerance and microstructural questions interesting, but the long-term stability remains a concern.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka's first perovskite sensitised cell, Park's solid-state cell and Snaith's mesostructured and thin-film cells are the usual credit chain. The three-person set is sensible, though the history of efficiency gains includes many other contributors.
assessment.maturity: The performance is firmly confirmed, but degradation and lead content limit the practical impact so far. The prize may be premature until stability and scale-up are demonstrated.
uncertainties: Operational stability and commercial viability are not yet shown.
The case is a materials and device advance rather than a discovery of a physical principle.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance in magnetic tunnel junctions, and then the large effect in MgO barriers, underpins magnetic read heads and magnetic random access memory. It is an important discovery and device invention whose interface physics is directly accessible by electron microscopy.
assessment.attribution: Miyazaki and Moodera reported the room-temperature effect in 1995, and Yuasa and others (and Parkin) achieved the coherent-tunnelling MgO result. The credit allocation is contested because Parkin and Djayaprawira, and theorists such as Butler and Mathon, are not on the list.
assessment.maturity: The technology is mature and in wide use. The related giant magnetoresistance already received the 2007 prize, so some committee members may see this as a follow-on rather than a new topic.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2007 prize for giant magnetoresistance.
Missing contributors to the MgO result, including theorists and the Parkin group.
Several independent discoveries make priority uncertain.
